The forklift operator was restacking fallen cartons from a damaged pallet in the shipping bay by hand. The task was being done while behind the plan or a deadline. Stage of the task: transport or handling material. Method in effect: SW-140 Manual Restacking of Damaged Pallets. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method calls for two people to restack a damaged pallet, but only one operator was in the bay at that hour and the trailer was due out. Equipment involved: A damaged wooden pallet and cartons in the shipping bay. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: damaged or broken. Detail: The pallet had a broken top board which is why the load had shifted. The object handled weighed 25 to 50 lb. Handling difficulty: bulky - hard to get arms around and no hand holds. It was held both hands, gripped underneath and held against the body. PPE in use: safety glasses, steel toe boots and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task. The event was not witnessed and was self reported later. Immediately before the event: squatting beside the damaged pallet with a carton at floor level, back turned toward the stack it was going onto. Body position at the moment: bent and twisted. At the moment of the event: the carton was raised to about chest height and the torso twisted to the right to place it on the stack behind, at which point a sharp pain was felt across the lower back. Immediately after the event: the carton was placed on the stack, the operator straightened up slowly and continued restacking more carefully, and the trailer was loaded on time. The injury arose from overexertion during manual handling. Load handled: 25 to 50 lb. The load was moved from floor level to chest height. It was held at about arm reach. Assist device: No assist device exists for this task. This was a one-person lift. Point of contact: lower back on the right side. Force applied from in front. Difference from a normal run of this task: The written method requires two people for a damaged pallet and only one operator was in the bay at that hour. Conditions at the point of injury: time or production pressure. Detail: The trailer was booked out within the hour and the bay was otherwise empty. The event occurred in beyond the scheduled shift end. Several consecutive days of overtime had been worked. It happened within roughly half an hour in. The forklift operator had performed this task before. No known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The restack could have waited for a second person, but that would have meant missing the trailer departure and no cover was available. At the scene, no first aid was given at the scene. No first aid was given at the scene. Notified: the supervisor. This happened the following day or later. Reason for the delay in reporting: the pain was mild at the time and was expected to settle overnight, and the trailer still had to be loaded. It was worse the following morning. Afterwards, nothing was secured. Work at the location continued unchanged. The forklift operator was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
